summary: Optimism over a possible US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz has driven equities to fresh records, with Brent dropping below $79 and Qatar confirming an interim proposal has been drafted. Meanwhile, the Fed held rates at 3.5–3.75% at its July meeting, though three FOMC members dissented in favor of a hike, keeping bond markets uneasy and real rates elevated.
tweet: Iran deal optimism pushed stocks to all-time highs and crushed oil, but three Fed hawks dissenting on hikes are keeping bonds under pressure.
